newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soyoil ends up on funds, world crop concerns.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soyoil ends up on funds, world crop concerns.

text.p: CBOT soyoil futures ended higher on Friday on heavy fund buying and on forecasts for dry weather in India and China, traders said.
Soymeal ended mixed with nearbys up on the lack of deliveries posted against the August and new crop down on forecasts for weekend rains in the U.S. Midwest.
Soymeal ended $3.30 per ton higher to $1.80 lower with August up $3.30 at $261.50. Soyoil closed 0.25 to 0.10 cent per lb higher with December up 0.17 at 22.96 cents.

"Soyoil is beginning to show more leadership," an oilseeds trader said. "The technical picture is looking strong," he added. "That's why the funds were in there. Now they're talking about the monsoon ending early in India."
Smith Barney meteorologist Jon Davis said in his weather update that monsoonal activity in India has started to diminish considerably.

"This is a very unusual situation to occur during the middle of August," Davis wrote. "It means one of two things. Either the monsoonal activity is taking a break and it will rebuild later in August or the monsoon is starting to retreat."
Davis also said no rain had fallen across the central and northern China agricultural areas in the past week.

"Stress is again starting to be a problem for developing beans while for the corn, it is too late for the crop to stage a comeback," Davis wrote. "It will remain dry across central and northern China the next few days before a frontal system moves across the region on Sunday and Monday."
Those weather forecasts led to ideas oil content will suffer. Lack of moisture late in the growing season tends to cut oil production, traders said. India and China are both major oilseed producers.
There was also talk of El Nino-related dryness in Indonesia and the Philippines.

The National Oilseed Processors Association monthly crush data lent support to soyoil. NOPA on Friday pegged soyoil stocks at 1.704 billion lbs, below the 1.747 billion reported last month and last year's 1.864 billion.

Funds bought at least 2,500 lots of soyoil on the day, keying off of technical signals. The December soyoil contract peaked just shy of 23.20 cents, a level traders pegged as a key technical point. They said funds had been trying to reach that level all day as there were reportedly buy stops above it.
"The recent high is 23.19 (cents) and that's also pretty close to the 50-day moving average," a technical trader said. "They went after them today and they'll probably get them Monday."

Domestic weather forecasts weighed on new crop soymeal futures. Forecasts called for widespread rains this weekend in the U.S. Midwest with coverage anywhere from 65 to 80 percent, meteorologists said.

On the day, Lind-Waldock bought 500 lots December soyoil, Cargill Investor Services and Refco Inc each bought 400 December and Smith Barney bought 500 December and sold 500 December and 200 September, traders said. E D & F Man International sold 200 December.
Commercials were largely on the sell-side. ADM sold 400 lots December, 200 October and 100 each August and September. Cargill Inc sold 500 December and 200 October, floor sources said.
In soymeal, Refco Inc bought 300 September while Smith Barney and Merrill Lynch each bought 200 September.
Soymeal futures volume was estimated by CBOT at 18,200 lots, against Thursday's 20,545. Soyoil volume was pegged at 18,600 lots, against Thursday's 14,125.
